Sl. Office
No Date Order Note
07 11.11.2024 Cgr, J
There is no representation for the petitioners.
As  per the proceedings sheet, even on 20.10.2020, none  appeared for the petitioners.
2. The present writ petition is filed aggrieved by

the  action of respondents in not giving opportunity to the petitioners to submit their objections and conduct 5A enquiry as contemplated under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 by considering their request as made in representation dated 05.03.2008 in pursuance to the proposed acquisition of their lands in an extent of Acres 0.67 cents in S.No.48/6 of Srikrishnapatnam Village, Rajanagaram Mandal, as arbitrary and illegal

. 
3. The learned Assistant Government Pleader referring to the counter filed on behalf of the respondents submits that the land of the petitioners was acquired for the purpose of excavation of Main canal from KM 2.688 to KM 6.550 under Venkatanagaram Pumping Scheme, for which the proposal was received for acquiring an extent of Acres 63.91 cents.

After necessary survey, draft notification under Section 4 was issued for an extent of Acres 63.91 cents, which was later on got reduced to Acres 38.10 cents in view of revision of the land acquisition proposals which was made to Sl. OFFICE
No DATE ORDER NOTE accommodate the requests of the farmers by reducing the width of the bund.

It is further stated that an errata had been issued confining the acquisition to an extent of Acres 38.10 cents and prepared draft notification and in view of the urgency, enquiry under Section 5A has been exempted by invoking Section 17 of the Act.

The award enquiry was conducted on 25.02.2007 and 80% of compensation was tendered to 39 land owners out of 47, who have attended the award enquiry and given consent for acquisition of their land to an extent of Acres 28.33 cents and later, they were paid full compensation as well.

It is further stated that the writ petitioners have not attended the award enquiry and therefore, the respondents have proceeded with award enquiry and even issued notices under Sections 9(1) & 10 and 9(3) & 10 of the Act fixing the date of enquiry on 19.04.2008 and later on, an award has been passed.
4. The learned counsel for petitioners on earlier occasion sought time to verify as to whether any cause survives in the writ petition.
Since there is no representation for the petitioners, the learned Assistant Government Pleader shall get instructions as to whether an award has been passed and compensation paid to the petitioners.
